title: Games, local search and genetic algorithms
subtitle: When an opponent answers back, and when the path does not matter — only the final state.

minimax.title: Minimax
minimax.body: In a zero-sum game two players alternate. MAX tries to maximise a score, MIN to minimise it. Minimax looks ahead to the leaves, scores them with an evaluation function, and backs values up: MAX nodes take the largest child, MIN nodes the smallest. The root value is the best MAX can guarantee against perfect play. Cost: bᵈ nodes.

ab.title: Alpha–beta pruning
ab.body: Alpha–beta carries two bounds: α, the best MAX is already assured, and β, the best MIN is already assured. When α ≥ β the remaining children cannot change the decision and are pruned. It returns the same value as minimax but evaluates fewer leaves: here 5 of 8, value 5. With perfect move ordering it searches about b^(d/2) nodes — doubling the depth you can afford.

hill.title: Local search: hill climbing and simulated annealing
hill.body: For timetabling or n-queens the path is irrelevant. Hill climbing moves to the best neighbouring state until none is better; it gets stuck on local maxima, plateaus and ridges. Simulated annealing sometimes accepts a worse move with probability e^(−Δ/T), where the temperature T falls over time: early on it explores, later it settles. Random restarts also help.
hill.steps: Current cost 10; a neighbour has cost 12 (Δ = 2). Temperature T = 4. Probability of accepting the worse move.

ga.title: Genetic algorithms
ga.body: A genetic algorithm keeps a population of candidate solutions (bit strings). Each generation: selection (fitter individuals are more likely parents, e.g. roulette wheel), crossover (swap tails at a random cut) and mutation (rare bit flips). Here it maximises f(x) = x² over 5-bit strings (optimum 31² = 961); after 30 generations of 10 individuals the best fitness reaches 961 (optimum 961).

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Minimax backs up values; alpha–beta prunes without changing them.
  • Local search ignores the path; annealing escapes local optima; GAs evolve populations.

ex.title: Try it
ex.body: Change the leaf values and watch which branches get pruned. Good ordering (best move first) prunes the most; bad ordering prunes nothing.
